notes:
Atkin page 8 continues (3.11) with P=product p_i^theta_i and deduces positive density of coefficients divisible by each power of 13. It then contrasts the partition function and other forms of half-integral dimension, whose M- and R-results contain an additional unknown constant. The author reports finding thirteen accidents and concludes divisibility of p(n) by 13^13 on a set of positive density. The two occurrences of 13 have different roles, as the source explicitly jokes. Section 4, The cases q=17,19,and 23, reports analogous computations among the primes 17,19,23,29,31,37, using methods cited as ATKIN(1967). It attributes the extension of tests to reusable computer subroutines. No external source was consulted.

S048-POSITIVE-DENSITY: Choose alpha distinct primes p_i other than 13, with theta_i as in the recurrence argument on scan47. Equation (3.7) propagates each zero modulo 13 to the normalized coefficient t_alpha(p_i^theta_i). Coprime multiplicativity obtained by iterating (3.9) then makes t_alpha(Pn) divisible by 13^alpha whenever (n,P)=1. Since c(13^alpha) is a unit, this gives (3.11). The subset of indices m=13^alpha Pn with (n,P)=1 has density phi(P)/(13^alpha P^2)>0, establishing the claimed positive lower density under the stated input identities. This reasoning checks the consequence, not the underlying theorems.
